title: Install only scripts that guidance, hooks or the Dashboard reach

intentCoverage.report:
**Verdict: Caught.** At revision `287001929d9300897bc377746d27cfc4baff29d2`, the maintained wait test caught a regression that scheduled a poll before fetching a publication already on the remote. The check covers a watched path resumed with the deadline from the prior result. It confirms the immediate-continuation proof recorded for SEED-423#remove-unreached-distribution-code in Slice 8 and source review P44.

In an isolated checkout, I changed line 163 of `Distribution/src/skills/dough-execute-plan/scripts/wait-for-publication.mjs` from `let pause = retained === null;` to `let pause = true;`. I ran the same guarded `scripts/test.sh Distribution/tests/skills/dough-execute-plan/continued-wait-for-publication.test.mjs` command before the fault, with the fault, and after restoring the file. The three cases passed at baseline and after restoration. With the fault, the immediate-continuation case at line 29 failed and the other two passed. The `continueBeforePolling` fixture raised “the continued wait reached the poll timer,” and the `onlyResult` assertion of empty stderr at line 147 of `Distribution/tests/support/wait-for-publication-fixture.mjs` caught it before the result comparison.

A separate real-Git scenario first confirmed the prior publication was recorded and a later one was already on the remote. With the fault, the CLI scheduled a 60,000 ms timer while `FETCH_HEAD` and the retained watched blob still identified the prior publication. With the original code restored, the same scenario fetched the later publication and returned the prior and later watched objects with the original deadline before scheduling a timer. The restored file hash and clean Git status matched the baseline. I removed the scratch checkout and kept the logs in `/tmp/open-dough-intent-423.xZq0ff`.

**Next proof action.** Retain the existing immediate-continuation case as proof for this path.

- **Test runtime.** Measured by the project runner at 2.7 seconds baseline, 2.1 seconds with the fault, and 2.4 seconds restored.
- **Human effort.** Unavailable because no separate human time was recorded.
- **Agent effort.** Unavailable because no separate active-agent time was recorded.


- **Invocation-to-report elapsed.** 166785 ms (measured), from 1795408310229 to 1795408477014 in Unix epoch ms. The end clock was sampled after writing the prepared report body.

**Disposition.** Caught at `287001929d9300897bc377746d27cfc4baff29d2` (Slice 8, source review P44). Keep the existing immediate-continuation test. No new proof work is needed.
